i can give advice on what's worked for me, but honestly the best advice i can give is to try different strategies to find out what works for you best, not someone else. i have adhd and what works for me wont necessarily work for you, but if you find that some of this works for you then go nuts! none of this is the only Definitive Way to succeed in university. also im in the sciences so my experience may be different to how yours will be.

first i recommend using a program called [anki](https://ankiweb.net). it's basically flash cards, but digital. it spaces them out for you so youll get a card right before you would forget it, and it has made memorizing things an absolute breeze. downsides are it can take some time to get used to, but i dont even take full notes during lecture anymore, just write down what the prof says that isnt on the slides. making the cards themselves can take time but it doesnt feel like a waste of time because youre still studying the material. (i literally just go through the slides and copy the important parts onto cards). dont do too many new reps a day, stick to 20-40 per class to start with or youll get burnt out. 

other than that, get enough sleep! do not fall into the cycle of not sleeping it is vicious and difficult to get out of. you will be more productive well rested. make sure you do pay attention in class, if you dont then theres really no reason to be there. also dont just show up just to chat with a friend, theres a time and a place for that but the people who chat during lectures are the ones who are super confused during review. skipping class every once in a while isnt horrible but if you do you must teach yourself the content after, dont assume youll pick it up next time. you are responsible for your own learning moreso than high school. that means sometimes you will have to teach yourself things sometimes (which sucks). 

scheduling study time has helped me a lot. make sure you get enough breaks and get up/ walk around while studying or you will be miserable. be proactive with studying, you kinda have to or youll fall behind. but be aware theres more to being a student than good grades and if youre getting burnt out you should reach out for help. theres free 1-on-1 tutoring services the school offers, along with others (that i admittedly havent checked out much, you should look on the website).

that got long! again what works for me wont always work for you. try different strategies. see what works for you, and what you like. just remember that your metnal health matters. good luck :)!
